description: Weathered sandstone sanctuary tower on a laterite platform, partly collapsed, with carved lintels and a false door on three faces.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Squat sandstone sanctuary tower of stacked receding tiers on a broad laterite platform, one doorway with a heavily carved lintel and flanking colonnettes, blank false doors on the other three faces, upper tiers partly collapsed with fallen blocks scattered across the platform, short flight of steps up the platform front, remains of a low enclosing wall Materials: Warm grey-brown sandstone weathered rough and pitted, dark red porous laterite platform blocks, orange lichen and black biological staining, soil and grass in the joints, sharp fresh breaks on the fallen blocks.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93 -- not a pass self-score. Band table 0.035 / 0.024 of height against the proxy with the whole tower inside 0.03 H; rendered tones inside the plate's probed range; turntable gate 0.000-0.005% enclosed background at four azimuths. 11,188/16,000 triangles, 11/16 draw calls, 8/16 materials, 11/16 unique geometries, 5 canvas textures at 6.7 MB, factory ~90 ms. Every fallen block passes the four-corner raycast support check.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 10.60 x 9.00 x 12.00 m -- re-declared FROM the Meshy proxy's bounding box this build (1.68 x 1.429 x 1.90 units at 9 m: 10.6 across, 12.0 deep, the 1.4 m of extra depth being the stair bay projecting off one face). Area-weighted band comparison against the proxy gives mean |delta width| 0.035 and |delta depth| 0.024 of height (second build 0.041 / 0.055), with bands 3-9 -- the whole tower -- inside 0.03 H and no band past the 0.12 flag.
featureReviews.notes: The tower stack was read off the proxy's +Z orthographic depth map (96.7 px/m) for the door, plinth and body, then CORRECTED by the band table for the roof: the map put the entablature at 5.90-6.75 and band 6 (5.4-6.3) measured -0.094 H against it; the table puts the flare from 5.05 and the widest band at 6.05-6.60, and the second tier stepping in to 5.1 m, which measured -0.025 / +0.009. The residual is in bands 0-2, the platform-and-enclosure zone (-0.04 / -0.10 / -0.08 in width), where the 5-95 percentile is dominated by the platform top's area rather than its edge and the proxy's enclosure is open on the stair side where the plate shows it closed; the platform's outer extent is the proxy's own bounding box.

featureReviews.evidence: Top ring authored as a PARTIAL ring with the (+X, -Z) corner gone and that corner's acroterion missing below it; thirty-six blocks authored one by one -- six on the ring, six heaped inside it, five slid down the ledges under the fallen corner, sixteen on the platform, one fallen into a gap in the wall, one on the wall, one on the ground by the stair -- each with its own yaw, non-uniform scale and one of five measured tones; the enclosure wall is fifty-six individual instanced blocks in running bond with members missing; a raycast from every block's four bottom corners (world space) reports every corner within 5 cm of support, the one ground block excepted.
featureReviews.notes: The second build's textured-box enclosure read as brickwork against the plate's plainly individual blocks with an irregular broken top; the wall blocks now carry one cell of the coursing tile each and one of five laterite tones. The support tool was checking instance corners in node-local space against world geometry, which this build's 0.70 m z-shift exposed; it applies the node's world matrix now. Two ledge blocks and one wall-top block overhung on the first pass and were moved onto the ledge that exists (the plan is stepped, so a ledge corner is cut back).

featureReviews.evidence: The doorway is a real 1.19 x 2.27 m opening recessed 1.05 m into the mass -- the lower body slab's plan carries the notch -- with the body's own stone for reveals and a dark cell at the back; each face carries two ringed colonnettes (four collars, square base and capital) in front of jambs, a 2.62 m carved lintel and a naga-frame pediment from a relief atlas, and the three false doors are proud leaves with a rib and a lock rail; both roof tiers repeat the whole aedicule in miniature on every face from the same instanced geometries (12 door units, 12 relief plates, 11 blind leaves).
featureReviews.notes: The second build's door was 1.90 m wide and a proud dark panel on a solid face; the proxy's depth map has a 1.19 m opening going into the mass, and a recess is what reads as a doorway from the three-quarter view. The lintel relief and the naga frame were recorded then as below the resolvable band; they are the darkest, busiest band on the face at any distance the door is read from, and are authored as procedural ornament in the plate's grammar (foliage scroll, kala medallion, beaded rails, nested flame-scalloped arches) bound as map and bumpMap. Not a copy of the plate's particular carving.

featureReviews.evidence: Harness transfer PROBED on a flat-tile render of this build (a +Z face renders at 1.0-1.05x its authored albedo, 315-view sides at 0.85x, lit tops at 1.25x) and every tone authored as the plate's value over the tile's mean: the +Z sandstone faces render at luma 88-110 against the plate's 76-128, the 315 sides at 53-91 against 76-90, the laterite at 64-75 against 91 lit / ~60 in shade. Laterite as 1.07 x 0.40 m blocks with 9 cm joints at 0.30, eroded arrises and 1,700 pits; sandstone sides with blurred black washes; ledge tops SPLIT onto their own material carrying orange and pale lichen crusts over soil and moss; carved relief atlas; five rubble tones; grass tufts.
featureReviews.notes: Two wrong tiles preceded the shipped one and both were caught by probing rather than by eye: the first ran 34 black washes plus 20 wide ones, averaged ~0.45 of clean and rendered the lit faces at luma 36-69; the second was right in tone but scattered 44 small lichen clusters over every face and read as confetti. The shipped sandstone tile runs 12 washes at 0.75 and 5 wide at 0.38, and the lichen moved to the ledge material as 34 dense patches per tile. The laterite went #9A6A50 -> #8C6852 after the lit +Z face rendered (137, 91, 65), too orange against the plate's purple-brown.

name: Khmer Stone Sanctuary
notes: An Isan ruin, so it is authored as partly collapsed with fallen blocks on the platform rather than as an intact building -- ruination is the state it is actually found in and is what distinguishes it. It is deliberately a separate asset from the Thai prang even though both descend from the Khmer tower form: this one is squat, dark, rough sandstone on a red laterite platform, where the prang is tall, slim, pale and encrusted with porcelain, and the two read as entirely different objects. The false doors on three of the four faces are a genuine Khmer feature, not an omission. Declared at 9 m tall, above the building-part category's 8 m prior. Width re-declared 12 -> 10.6 m on 2026-09-02 from the Meshy proxy: its bounding box is 1.68 x 1.429 x 1.90 units with the 9 m height, so 1.68 x 9 / 1.429 = 10.6 m across and 1.90 x 9 / 1.429 = 12.0 m deep -- the extra 1.4 m of depth is the stair BAY projecting off one face, which the plate shows standing proud of the platform between two cheeks rather than cut into it. The platform proper is 10.6 m square. No destruction groups: the collapse is modelled into the geometry, and the prop does not break apart further at runtime.
